title: Which number is called idli-vada first for two numbers?
description: In the idli-vada game the first number found in both lists of multiples is where both calls happen. The first number is found for four and six, and then for seven and eleven. Keeko doubts this and wants to multiply four and six, which gives a number that is not the first.
teaching_notes: One idea: the first idli-vada number is the first number found in both lists of multiples. Watch for students who multiply the two numbers and take the product as the first, when a smaller common multiple comes sooner.

source: Find the first number for which idli-vada will be called out, for 4 and 6, and for 7 and 11.
video_script.why: The child has used lists of multiples for torans and gajak days and now applies the same list-and-match method in a game.
video_script.substitution: List the multiples of each number and take the first number found in both lists.
video_script.anchor: Two rows of multiples written one under the other, with the idli row and the vada row labelled, as in the game from the earlier class.
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko finds the first idli-vada number for four and six by multiplying them to get twenty four, but twelve comes sooner in both lists.
video_script.payoff_line: The first idli-vada numbers are twelve and seventy seven

final_answer.spoken: twelve for the first pair and seventy seven for the second pair

never_show: 24 as the first idli-vada number, marked right
maths_rules: multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12, 16; multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18; the first number in both is 12
multiples of 7: 7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42, 49, 56, 63, 70, 77; multiples of 11: 11, 22, 33, 44, 55, 66, 77; the first number in both is 77
slip: 4 × 6 = 24 is in both lists but 12 comes first, since 12 = 3 × 4 = 2 × 6
for 7 and 11 the product 77 is the first, because they share no factor other than 1
video_script.design: One idea: the first idli-vada number is the first number in both lists of multiples. The two lists for each pair stay on the board together.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>In the idli-vada game, two numbers are chosen. Players say idli on the multiples of the first number, and vada on the multiples of the second.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>On a number that is in both lists, they say idli-vada.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Find the first idli-vada number for four and six, and for seven and eleven.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Keeko thinks the first number comes by multiplying four and six, which gives twenty four.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Twenty four does get both calls.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>But the question asks for the first number, and twelve comes sooner. Multiplying gives a number in both lists, not always the first.
